paragraphs.text: dsh-logger-channels gives a DSH profile a visible log sink
# dsh-logger-channels
dsh-logger-channels gives a DSH profile a visible log sink: named channels that receive every `ctx.l
ogger` record from the framework and all plugins, so runtime log output reaches the operator instead
of ending only in the host's in-memory buffers.

- Named channels: stderr, stdout, and size-rotated files, each with its own level threshold
- One li

ne per record in a fixed shape
- No tool surface and no config files of its own; channels are declar
ed in the process env and/or a cordis config layer
## Installation
dsh-logger-channels is an out-of-tree plugin for a dsh profile. Install it with the dsh plugin comma

Configuration is layered: built-in defaults, the `LOGGER_CHANNELS_*` process-env block, and a cordis
config layer (see below).
## Configuration
One variable per channel declares it (`TYPE`); the rest attach to the declared channel and are optio
variable per channel declares it (`TYPE`); the rest attach to the declared channel and are optional:
| Variable | Required | Meaning |
| `LOGGER_CHANNELS_<NAME>_TYPE` | yes | declares channel `<name>` = the lowercased `<NAME>`; the val

ue is `stderr`, `stdout`, or `file` |
| `LOGGER_CHANNELS_<NAME>_PATH` | file only | output file path

(parent directories are created) |
| `LOGGER_CHANNELS_<NAME>_MINLEVEL` | no | numeric level thresho

ld: 0 = error only, 1 = +info, 2 = +warn, 3 = +debug (default 2) |
| `LOGGER_CHANNELS_<NAME>_COLORS`

| no | ANSI color level: `false` or 1-3 (default `false`) |
| `LOGGER_CHANNELS_<NAME>_MAXLENGTH` |

no | per-line truncation in characters (default 10240) |
| `LOGGER_CHANNELS_<NAME>_MAXBYTES` | no (f

ile) | size that triggers rotation, in bytes (default 10485760) |
| `LOGGER_CHANNELS_<NAME>_KEEP` |
no (file) | number of rotated generations to keep (default 5) |
Example:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The `<NAME>` segment of the variable name is uppercase letters and digits only, and the channel name
is its lowercased form; the channel name must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`, so e.g. `LOGGER_CHANN
ELS_1APP_TYPE` declares no channel, and a lowercase segment such as `LOGGER_CHANNELS_app_TYPE` match
es nothing at all. A key other than `TYPE` on a name that no `TYPE` variable declares is ignored, as
are unknown keys in the namespace.
The level numbers follow cordis's verbosity ladder, not a severity ladder: `ERROR=0, INFO=1, WARN=2,
DEBUG=3`. Note that `INFO` sorts numerically *before* `WARN`, the opposite of the log4j/Python seve
rity convention. The config layer's `minLevel` uses the same numbering.
### Config layer (cordis patch)
An optional config layer sits on top of the env block: a patch entry targeting the plugin id `dsh-lo
gger-channels` (the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, the user-global `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml`, or a `-
-patch` overlay) carries a `config` object with one key, `channels` (a map of channel name to `chann
el`, `minLevel`, `colors`, `maxLength`, `path`, `maxBytes`, `keep`). Every key is optional.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- One precedence chain: config value > env value > built-in default; keys the layer omits resolve as

the env block, so `config: {}` (or no entry) is exactly the env-only behavior.
- A patch targets a
row by id and replaces its whole config - no deep merge, so a layer that overrides one field restate
s the fields it keeps (layer order: the plugin's own default entry, the profile patch, the user-glob

al patch, any `--patch` overlay).
- Channels are the union of both layers; per key, the config layer

wins.
- Config errors (unknown channel type, a file channel without `path`, an out-of-range value)
fail the plugin entry at apply time with a labeled error, and the profile does not start.
## Line format
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Fields, in order: wall-clock timestamp (UTC), `#sn` (per-boot sequence number; resets on restart), l
evel, logger name, body. In the body, an Error as the first argument renders its stack; the body is
subject to the channel's `maxLength`.
## Limits
- File channels rotate on size: when a write would push the file past `maxBytes`, the live file is r
enamed to `.1` (the newest generation), older generations shift to `.2` ... `.keep`, and the oldest
generation is dropped. Files are appended to, and the size counter is seeded from the existing file

on open, so rotation continues across restarts.
- Runtime write failures never propagate to the host
: a channel that cannot write (missing permissions, a full disk, a failed rotation) goes quiet and d
rops its own subsequent writes while the other channels keep working. A full disk is therefore silen

t on the affected channel - watch file modification times, not the log stream.
- `stdout` is a share
d stream: in profiles where stdout carries a structured protocol, do not configure a `stdout` channe

l; stream ownership is the operator's to coordinate.
- When at least one channel is declared, the pl
ugin logs one status line (level INFO) on start naming each channel and its threshold.
